note: Divergence ratchets for scripts/flix-spec-conformance.sh. Lower them as divergences are fixed; never raise one without saying why in the commit message. The measurement is only comparable against the flix-spec inputs recorded below -- a different pin or fixture revision is a different question, not a regression. Read fixturesAgreeing together with depthPercent: a high agreement count at low depth is the number to distrust, because an unmapped node is skipped rather than compared, so a map that maps little agrees with almost everything.

oracle_conformance.comment: Measured against flix-spec 0.77.1 (Flix v0.77.0, 147 fixtures), report schemaVersion 7. Migration step 1 moved the pin with no code change: 75/147, 107 divergences, depth 42% (907 of 2165) -- 21 of the rise from 81 in the 9 new fixtures, the old 138 net +5, and depth flat because normalisation removed wrappers this grammar was already skipping. Step 2 cut elide to CommentList alone: 129 divergences, depth 41% (886 of 2180), 108 unmapped. All 22 new divergences come from AnnotationList (5) and ModifierList (13, plus their interaction): the contract only drops those lists when empty, and the old local elide was also hiding the non-empty ones, which this grammar has no node for (declPrefix is annotation* modifier*). They are real divergences, not a regression; annotationList/modifierList rules with dropWhenEmpty close them. Removing Expr.Expr, Pattern.Pattern, QName, UseOrImportList, Expr.Statement and Type.Apply changed nothing measurable: each sits below an unmapped expr/type/qname node where the walk already stops, so their divergences surface only once steps 4-5 map those. Step 2b split declPrefix into annotationList? modifierList? (annotation+ / modifier+), mapped onto AnnotationList and ModifierList: 129 -> 107 divergences, 886 -> 916 nodes compared, depth 42%. Unmapped rose 108 -> 112 only because the walk now reaches four more type nodes it used to stop short of. Then the projection keyed nodes by labelled alternative (neutral), and every primaryExpr alternative was labelled and mapped (literal, string, interpolation, hole, intrinsic, static, unit, paren, ascription, tuple): 97/147 agreeing, 93 divergences, 1009 of 2180 compared (depth 46%). Token-only leaves used to project as a childless primaryExpr that the map could only drop, shifting every later sibling. Unmapped rose to 132 because the walk now reaches much further. Then Operator nodes were synthesised for the unary and binary labels, which now map onto Expr.Unary/Expr.Binary, and the three cast labels were split and mapped: 96/147, 94 divergences, 1111 compared (depth 51%), 118 unmapped. The +1 is two real differences the deeper walk now reaches -- an unterminated block comment lexes as / * here but as one error token in Flix, and unchecked_cast holds `T \ ef` as one EffectAnnotatedType where Flix flattens type and effect -- less one fixed (checked_cast now Expr.CheckedTypeCast). Then the type labels: operators synthesised for the unary and binary type labels (Type.Unary/Type.Binary, the arrow included), ApplyType split so only an applied type maps to Type.Apply, EffectAnnotatedType flattened as the reference places type and effect side by side, and every primaryType alternative labelled -- with VariableType moved ahead of QNameType, since qname also matches a lone lowercase name and ANTLR had been parsing every type variable as one: 100/147, 88 divergences, 1175 compared (depth 54%), 115 unmapped. Then typeAndEffect was flattened (it had become the top stop once EffectAnnotatedType was): 108/147, 76 divergences, 1237 compared (depth 57%), 101 unmapped.

recovery_conformance.comment: This grammar declares no recoveryMarkers, so there is no error-recovery vocabulary for the lane to compare and it stands down with that as the recorded reason. ANTLR's own recovery inserts error nodes the parse tree does not name, so declaring markers needs a deliberate decision about which of our rules stand for recovery rather than syntax -- not a guess.

source_invariants.comment: document-shape passes. token-positions (new in flix-spec 0.77.x) stands down for the same reason token-accounting does: the projection emits no tokens. The vocabulary checks stand down because a projection map is in play, and token-accounting stands down because the projection emits no token leaves. That is not laziness: this grammar routes comments to the COMMENTS and DOC_COMMENTS channels, and off-channel tokens never appear in the parse tree, so emitting what the tree holds would silently omit every comment and fail a check that should have stood down. Splicing the off-channel tokens back into position would let this consumer pass the one oracle-free check in the suite, which neither other structural consumer can.

diagnostic_conformance.comment: The projection writes an empty diagnostics list for every fixture, so the lane stands down. Emitting ANTLR lexer and parser errors (migration step 3) makes it measurable.
